title: Affine localization exact sequences and their completed comparison
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subsetneq A$ be an ideal, and assume $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an ideal $K$, put $\Gamma_K(N)=\{x\in N:K^r x=0\text{ for some }r\geq0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], and write $R\Gamma_K$ for its right derived functor and $H_K^j(M)=H^j(R\Gamma_K(M[0]))$. Write $L^{\wedge_I}=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(L\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I^n)$ for derived $I$-adic completion: the derived tensor is computed using a K-flat resolution, and the derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] using the mapping fibre of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the termwise products of a complex-level model of the tower. Use these derived-functor models and their natural completion maps, not arbitrary maps between abstract choices of cones. For every ideal $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ with $V(J)\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, put $V=X\setminus V(J)$, $C=(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}$ and $D=(R\Gamma(U,\mathcal F|_U))^{\wedge_I}$, where $V(K)=\{\mathfrak p:K\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ and global sections are Zariski module sections [pqf-def-cohomology]. There is a natural commutative diagram with exact rows $H_J^0(M)\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow\Gamma(V,\mathcal F|_V)\longrightarrow H_J^1(M)\longrightarrow0$ and $H^0(C)\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow H^0(D)\longrightarrow H^1(C)\longrightarrow0$. Its vertical arrows are $H^0(\alpha_J)$, $\mathrm{id}_M$, $\beta_V$, and $H^1(\alpha_J)$, with $\alpha_J$ the completion map followed by the natural identification $(R\Gamma_J(M[0]))^{\wedge_I}\cong C$. The map $\beta_V$ is induced by completion followed by the inverse of the completed restriction isomorphism $D\xrightarrow{\sim}(R\Gamma(V,\mathcal F|_V))^{\wedge_I}$. For $V'\subseteq V$ with $U\cap V(I)\subseteq V'$, these maps satisfy $\beta_{V'}\circ\mathrm{res}_{V,V'}=\beta_V$.
